statement.excerpt: It requires endless pre-training, post-training and script-based MacGuffins to do tasks with mathematically-guaranteed hallucinations that burn more tokens, raising costs on customers who are already in mutiny less than a quarter into being forced to pay a cost that is already unprofitable.

already in mutiny less than a quarter
a cost that is already unprofitable
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a causal chain connecting continuing model development and error handling to additional tokens, higher customer bills, customer resistance, and loss-making service.
I read endless as an ongoing requirement, rather than literally infinite computation.
Mathematically guaranteed hallucinations means errors cannot be eliminated across the relevant tasks. It does not mean every answer must be wrong.
The preceding discussion suggests modeled gross margins on OpenAI and Anthropic customer usage. It does not identify an observed company-wide net margin.
The three months preceding publication bound the claimed recent pricing experience. They do not establish when any particular customer began paying.
Mutiny means documented customer resistance, cancellations, spending restrictions, or migration prompted by charges.
criteria.support_condition: Technical and operational evidence establishes the claimed necessities, and matched customer and provider records connect them to extra tokens, higher bills, resistance within three months of the relevant pricing change, and negative service gross margins.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence directly disproves a necessary link in that chain for the stated scope. A cheaper isolated task, a positive margin on another product, or an error-free individual answer would not suffice.

The paper distinguishes statistical error pressure from incentives to answer rather than abstain. This limits a blanket interpretation of inevitability, but does not test the claimed billing and margin consequences.
